```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 4,
  fig.align = "center",
  fig.retina = 2,
  out.width = "100%",
  cache.extra = packageVersion("interactmeta")

```

This article follows [`vignette("cams")`](cams.html). It contrasts CAMS with
DA, AD, and SWADA on the same prepared REACT `des` object
[@panaro2026subgroup; @stern2020react]. Those three are different constructions,
not alternative CAMS likelihoods.

DA pools each subgroup then subtracts; AD pools within-trial contrasts; SWADA
applies a common weighting principle so DA's subgroup series can align with AD's
interaction [@panaro2026subgroup]. CAMS uses information fractions and orthogonal
$(m_j, g_j)$ blocks [@panaro2025cams].

## REACT `steroids` (mixed subgroup design)

Prepare the same design as in [`vignette("cams")`](cams.html):

```{r load, cache = TRUE}
library(interactmeta)
library(metafor)

steroids_es <- escalc(
  measure = "OR",
  ai = treat.events, bi = treat.total - treat.events,
  ci = cont.events, di = cont.total - cont.events,
  data = steroids
)
des <- ifrac(steroids_es, reference = "Non-IMV")
```

The design object matches [`vignette("cams")`](cams.html): same `reference`,
`big_var` placeholders, and optional `contrast` / `include_interaction` via
[`?ifrac`]. Remap trial or modifier columns with `trial`, `subgroup`, or
`modifier` when names differ from `study` / `level`.

```{r fit-sensitivity, cache = TRUE}
sens <- interactmeta::sensitivity(
  des,
  reference = "Non-IMV",
  method = "REML"
)
```

[`?sensitivity`] fits DA, AD, SWADA, and CAMS on one table by default. Trim
with `constructions = c("da", "ad")`, remap columns via `trial` / `subgroup`,
or pass an existing [`interactmeta`] from `cams()` instead of a data frame.
Arguments in `...` (for example `method`, `tau.prior`, `silent`) are forwarded
to each construction fitter.

## Interaction $\gamma$

Under default random-effects weights on this mixed table, DA need not match AD,
SWADA, and CAMS, which pool the same within-trial contrasts for $\gamma$ here.

```{r compare-int}
interactmeta::compare(
  sens,
  estimand = "interaction",
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  type = "Overall"
)
```

`compare()` on a sensitivity object accepts `estimand = "modifiers"` or
`"combined"` as well as `"interaction"`. Use `type = "Prediction"` for
prediction rows where supported, `exponentiate = TRUE` on log-scale outcomes,
and see [`?compare`] for interval formatting. Passing multiple fits directly
(without `sensitivity()`) still works for pairwise CAMS comparisons.

## Study weights (SWADA principle)

```{r weights}
interactmeta::compare_weights(sens$fits$da, sens$fits$ad, sens$fits$swada)
```

The table has class `interactmeta_compare_weights` and a `plot()` method
(`xlim` rescales the weight axis). For CAMS trial-level information fractions
on the same studies, use `compare_ifrac()` instead of `compare_weights()`.

IV-only trials can dominate DA weights for the IMV series while carrying little
weight in AD, SWADA, and CAMS interaction pooling (see
[`vignette("cams")`](cams.html) on mixed `steroids` designs).

## What CAMS adds

Contribution curves and grey shrinkage forests require a CAMS fit ([`?cams`]).

```{r contribution, fig.height = 5, cache = TRUE}
plot(sens$fits$cams, type = "contribution", ylim = c(0, 4), exponentiate = TRUE)
```

Beyond `ylim`, the contribution view accepts `exponentiate`, `at` / `ifrac`
(reporting fraction), and ggplot styling via [`?plot.interactmeta`]. Forest and
heterogeneity views use the same `plot()` method with other `type` values (see
[`vignette("cams")`](cams.html)).

## Complete-table illustration (`respire_age`)

On a complete subgroup table (every trial reports both strata), DA and AD can
still disagree when inverse-variance weights differ. RESPIRE age strata
[@panaro2026subgroup]:

```{r respire-sens, cache = TRUE}
sens_respire <- interactmeta::sensitivity(
  respire_age,
  reference = "<65",
  subgroup = "subgroup",
  method = "REML",
  constructions = c("da", "ad", "swada", "cams")
)

interactmeta::compare(
  sens_respire,
  estimand = "interaction",
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  type = "Overall"
)
```

`respire_age` uses `study` and `subgroup` rather than `level`; `sensitivity()`
remaps via `subgroup = "subgroup"`. The explicit `constructions` vector is
optional when you want all four fits; priors and `method` in `...` behave as in
the `steroids` run above.
